subject: Private deployment: cust. keys, operator access windows & DPA fit
messages:
From: Angela Collins <angela.collins@heliosoft.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: legal@heliosoft.com, sanjay.patel@heliosoft.com
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: BYOK & operator access clarification

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is drafting the DPA annex for a private VPC deployment and a couple of items need clarifying before we proceed:

1) Key custody model: we need to confirm Redwood's operational expectations when customers provide their own CMKs (BYOK). Will your operators ever be able to export/decrypt customer keys?
2) Operator access windows: do you require breakglass access for incidents? If so, what's the approval/notification flow and audit evidence you can provide?
3) Subprocessors: for private deployments hosted in our cloud VPC, which Redwood subprocessors (if any) will still touch telemetry/logs or metrics that could include pseudonymized identifiers?

Attached is a short list of specific DPA questions from our legal team. Can we get answers by EOD Thursday so we can include them in the draft?

Best,
Angela Collins
Head of Security, HelioSoft

Attachments: HelioSoft-DPA-questions-v1.pdf
From: logan_wright@redwood.com
To: Angela Collins <angela.collins@heliosoft.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: BYOK & operator access clarification

Angela — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and we'll follow with a redlined annex where useful: 

1) Key custody: customer-managed keys (BYOK) remain under the customer's KMS/HSM control. Redwood never exports customer private key material. Our runtime integrates with customer KMS via an in-region key-encryption workflow; we only receive wrapped keys or use KMS signing/unwrap operations per configured policies.

2) Operator access: for private deployments (VPC or on-prem), operators do not have default access to customer data or plaintext. Breakglass access is supported only in documented emergency scenarios and requires: written customer approval (pre-authorized emergency contacts) OR an approved legal escalation plus a time-limited session recorded with session replay and captured to your audit bucket. We keep an operator action log, and can provide attestations and session recordings on request.

3) Subprocessors: for pure VPC-hosted private deployments, Redwood subprocessors that provide managed control plane services (billing, observability ingestion endpoint) may process metadata (route-level metrics, error codes, token counts). We can provide a minimized telemetry feed that strips identifiers and use onshore subprocessors per contract.

I'll loop in Priyom to cover the technical audit artifacts (keystore handshake, evidence we can deliver), and Kim to handle DPA wording and a proposed annex.

Next steps proposed:
- Redwood to send a short annex template and a keystore access matrix by Thursday EOD (we aim to include: allowed ops, breakglass gating, artifact list).
- HelioSoft to indicate if they require operator sessions pushed to their S3/GCS bucket and the preferred KMS vendor.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-keystore-access-matrix.xlsx
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Angela Collins <angela.collins@heliosoft.com>, logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private deployment: BYOK & operator access clarification

Hey Angela — technical follow-up with how the handshake works and the evidence package we'll provide: 

- BYOK integration: Redwood supports direct KMS API calls (e.g., AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). We never persist unwrapped key material. For HSM-backed keys we support envelope encryption where the model-serving process calls your KMS to unwrap per-request.
- Operator controls: operator identities are bound to short-lived SSO sessions. Any emergency escalation requires a two-person approval (on-call + engineering manager) and is time-limited to 30 minutes by default; we capture keystrokes, commands, and a timestamped session video.
- Evidence artifacts we can deliver (sample list): session logs (ndjson), audit trail export (CSV), TLS cert fingerprints, KMS audit events (redacted), and a signed attestation of no-export.

I attached a sample access matrix (roles -> allowed ops -> artifact produced). If HelioSoft prefers, we can rotate the default 30-minute window to 15 or require an explicit DocuSign sign-off for each breakglass.

Priyom Das
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: network-topology-vpc-onprem.png
From: Angela Collins <angela.collins@heliosoft.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: legal@heliosoft.com, sanjay.patel@heliosoft.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: BYOK & operator access clarification

Thanks Logan and Priyom — that's helpful. A few follow-ups from legal/security after reviewing your matrix: 

A) Please confirm in writing that Redwood will not request or hold plaintext customer model inputs or outputs outside of the customer's VPC except for transient memory in the inference runtime. We need this in the DPA annex.
B) For breakglass: HelioSoft policy requires pre-authorization of at least two named contacts and a post-incident attestation within 48 hours that details why access was exercised. Can Redwood commit to 48-hour attestation and provide the session video and audit log within that window?
C) Subprocessor minimization: Can Redwood provide a list of control-plane subprocessors that will be in-scope for the private deployment, and confirm whether any of them are located outside the US?

Attached is our DPA question set with specific clause language suggestions; legal flagged a potential redline around "support personnel" definition.

Appreciate the quick turn — aiming to finalize the annex before our procurement review next Tuesday.

— Angela

Attachments: HelioSoft-DPA-questions-v1.pdf
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Angela Collins <angela.collins@heliosoft.com>
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private deployment: BYOK & operator access clarification

Angela — copying formal responses that we will include in the DPA annex (we'll also send a redline PDF via DocuSign after you confirm):

1) No-export guarantee: Redwood confirms we will not export, persist, or retain plaintext customer data or key material outside of the customer's environment except for ephemeral memory necessary for inference. We will add a clause to the annex that references the runtime ephemeral memory model and the retention policy for transient buffers (max 120s).

2) Breakglass workflow and attestation: Redwood agrees to HelioSoft's 48-hour attestation timeline. Breakglass will be gated by two pre-authorized contacts (HelioSoft) plus Redwood on-call engineering approval. We will provide session video, command logs, and a signed post-incident statement within 48 hours. We will add this SLA into the annex and include penalties for missed attestation timelines in the enterprise addendum.

3) Subprocessors: enclosed is the current control-plane subprocessors list and their locations. We can commit to US-only subprocessors for your control-plane endpoints if requested; we'll include an explicit list in the annex and an obligation to notify you 30 days prior to adding a new subprocessor.

Next steps:
- Logan to send the draft annex (redline-enabled) and the updated access matrix by EOD Friday.
- Helio to confirm the names/emails of the two pre-authorized breakglass contacts and the preferred KMS vendor(s).

Kimberly Park
Head of Product, Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Links: DocuSign draft (will be created), Drive folder for audit artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cHelio-privdep-evidence
